name: How to Prepare Your Home for an Interior Refresh Project

step.name: Step 1: Define Your Scope and Expectations
step.text: Before any work begins, clearly outline what you want to achieve with your interior refresh. Are you looking to update paint, change flooring, or perhaps add new fixtures? A precise scope helps your contractor understand your vision and allows for accurate estimating and scheduling. This step is crucial for managing expectations and avoiding scope creep later on.

step.name: Step 2: Protect Your Belongings and Surfaces
step.text: Prior to the team arriving, remove or consolidate small, fragile items from the rooms being refreshed. Furniture that cannot be moved should be centrally located and covered to protect it from dust, paint, or debris. This protects your valuables and provides a clear workspace, preventing accidental damage to your cherished possessions or existing finishes.

step.name: Step 3: Address Any Underlying Surface Issues
step.text: Inspect walls and ceilings for any holes, cracks, or other surface damage. It’s important to repair these areas before painting or applying new finishes. Skipping surface preparation is a common mistake that can compromise the final look, as new paint won't hide imperfections but often highlight them.

step.name: Step 4: Confirm Material Selections and Drying Times
step.text: Make sure all paint colors, wallpaper, or other finish materials are finalized and, if possible, tested in your actual space. Don’t forget to factor in adequate drying and curing times, especially for paint or newly installed flooring. Rushing this can lead to issues like premature wear or lingering odors.

step.name: Step 5: Plan for Occupant Disruption
step.text: Consider how the project will affect daily life. If multiple rooms are being refreshed, you might need to temporarily relocate certain activities or even stay elsewhere for a short period. Clear communication with your contractor about access and work hours will help minimize inconvenience and ensure everyone is on the same page. Questions to Ask Before You Decide When planning an interior refresh, ask your potential contractor about their process for surface preparation, material quality, and how they handle cleanup. Inquire about their experience with similar projects in the Dallas–Fort Worth metroplex and if they foresee any challenges given your home's age or specific features. Understanding their approach to minimizing disruption is also key. Don't hesitate to ask for references from past clients who had similar work done.
